sections.name: metadata
sections.title: Browser tab title and description
sections.what: Sets the title shown in the browser tab and the short description of the site.
sections.why: Likely reason: the title identifies the app in the browser and in search results.

sections.name: RootLayout
sections.title: Outer page wrapper
sections.what: Builds the outer html and body wrapper, applies the font, and places the page content inside.
sections.why: Likely reason: Next.js needs one outer layout that wraps every page.
sections.watch_out: The language is fixed to English, so screen readers and spell checkers treat all text as English.

summary: The outer shell of every page: sets the browser tab title and description, loads the Inter font, and wraps each page in the body.
purpose: Gives the whole site its tab title, font and page wrapper.
why: Likely reason: the Next.js app folder requires one root layout that holds shared page setup.
how: Imports the page information type, the Inter font and the global styles. Creates the Inter font for Latin letters. Sets the title and description. Renders the html and body tags with the font applied and places the page content inside.
inputs: The page content passed in by Next.js, the Inter font from Google, and the metadata object.
outputs: The html and body wrapper used by every page, with the tab title and font applied.
risks: The font is fetched from Google during the build, so a build without internet access can fail. The language is fixed to English.
debug: If the font looks wrong, check the font import and whether the build machine can reach Google. If the tab title is wrong, check the metadata object.
